chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When he would pray the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) upon a woman and a man, he would place the woman first and delay the man; and when he would pray upon a slave and a free person, he would place the slave first and delay the free person; and when he would pray upon an elder and a younger person, he would place the younger first and delay the elder.
ai.seo_question: What is the order of rows in Shia funeral prayer for men, women, slaves, and children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific arrangement of rows during the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah), establishing a hierarchy where women precede men, slaves precede free persons, and the young precede the elderly. This ordering reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of social and spiritual precedence in ritual practice, distinguishing it from other juristic opinions that may prioritize gender or age differently.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you pray Salaat upon the woman and the man, so precede the woman and delay the man; and when you pray Salaat upon the slave and the free one, so preceded the slave and delay the free one; and when you pray Salaat upon the old and the young, so precede the young and delay the old’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd who has said the following: “

When abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, performed Salah (prayer) for a deceased man and a deceased woman, he (the Imam) would set forward woman, then the man. In the case of a slave and a free person, he (the Imam) would set forward the slave, then the free: and in the case of grown up and a minor, he set forward the minor then the grown up.”
